title: Hearing on Fair Chance Act challenges and successes
summary: The Council's Committee on Civil and Human Rights held an oversight hearing on the Fair Chance Act, which bars discrimination based on criminal record in employment and housing in New York City. The hearing examined enforcement trends, noting that Commission on Human Rights complaints on this basis fell from 138 in 2016 to 29 in fiscal year 2024, and explored ongoing challenges facing formerly incarcerated New Yorkers seeking jobs and housing. Witnesses invited included the Commission on Human Rights, legal aid groups, employers, real estate professionals and the public.
